source_caption:
The wolf scene in Fantastic Mr. Fox feels like more than a simple encounter. It’s almost as if Mr. Fox is finally facing a part of himself that he’s spent years trying to hide.

He has spent the film trying to live like a “civilized” fox—wearing a suit, paying bills, and being a responsible family man—while still feeling that wild side of himself underneath it all. The wolf represents that freedom and instinct he never completely lost.

When Mr. Fox sees the wolf, he doesn’t run from it. He calls it a “beautiful creature,” almost as if he’s finally accepting that part of himself instead of being ashamed of it.

That quiet fist raise at the end says more than words could. He knows he chose a different life, but he doesn’t have to deny who he is to live it.

source_details.title: Fantastic Mr. Fox
source_details.synopsis: Fantastic Mr. Fox is a 2009 adventure comedy film directed by Wes Anderson, who co-wrote it with Noah Baumbach, based on the 1970 novel by Roald Dahl. It stars George Clooney, Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Willem Dafoe, and Owen Wilson. In the stop-motion animated film, a spree of thefts led by Mr. Fox (Clooney) results in his family, and later his community, being hunted down by three farmers. Development on the project began in 2004 as a collaboration between Anderson and Henry Selick under Revolution Studios; by 2007, Revolution and Selick left for other projects. Work on Fantastic Mr. Fox was moved to 20th Century Fox, where production began in 2007 on Stage C of 3 Mills
